root_cause_label: Agent assumed TF checkpoint is raw float arrays; never correctly parsed format or implemented GPT-2 transformer inference
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent immediately assumed the TensorFlow checkpoint could be read as raw sequential floats, never implemented proper checkpoint parsing or the GPT-2 transformer forward pass, producing degenerate repetitive output throughout, and ultimately regressed to embedding dot-product similarity before submitting prematurely.
t_err_evidence: Step 2 writes the initial gpt2.c treating the checkpoint as a raw binary blob of sequential float arrays (emb, pos, ln1, qkv, proj, fc1, fc2, lnf, lm_head) without inspecting or parsing the actual TensorFlow checkpoint format, adopting a false premise about file structure that invalidates all weight loading.
t_commit_evidence: Step 9 rewrites gpt2.c to use only the last token's embedding for inference via forward-pass approximation that reads sequential floats from file but applies no real transformer layers, and uses embedding dot-products as logits — abandoning any attempt at correct transformer inference. From this point the approach cannot produce correct GPT-2 output regardless of subsequent edits.
t_surface_evidence: Step 5 run of ./a.out produces 'f f f f f f f f f 19 ĠRog ĠRog ĠRog ĠRog...' — clearly degenerate repetitive output confirming garbage weights from incorrect checkpoint parsing.
trigger_explanation: At step 2, the agent acts on an unverified assumption that the TF checkpoint binary is simply laid out as sequential raw float arrays (embeddings, positional embeddings, layer weights in order) without ever inspecting the actual file format, reading documentation, or verifying the layout. This false premise causes all subsequent weight loading to read garbage data.
forewarning_evidence: Step 5 output 'f f f f f f f f f 19 ĠRog ĠRog ĠRog ĠRog...' is a clear signal of garbage weights before t_commit=9. Step 12 output '#version: #version: #version:...' repeating similarly confirms ongoing parsing failure.
